answer.decision: Adopt regional token buckets with bounded global quotas and local burst allowance.
answer.action: Deploy one coordinated limiter per region using replicated tenant entitlements, divide each tenant's global quota into bounded regional allocations, permit a calibrated local burst allowance for sub-20-second spikes, and fail open only within strict per-tenant and regional safety caps during control-plane partitions.
reasons: Regional enforcement isolates heavy tenants while coordinating across instances, preventing the top 2 percent of tenants from exhausting shared capacity.
Local burst allowance accommodates observed short bursts of up to 4 times the five-minute average, reducing costly false throttling.
Request-path decisions remain regional, avoiding the 180 ms p99 cross-region control-plane latency of a centralized limiter.
Bounded regional allocations preserve availability during a partition or dependency outage without allowing unlimited quota overshoot.
Existing regional entitlement replicas supply quota inputs without requiring a global lookup.
The design can fit the operational constraint by introducing at most one new stateful dependency, unlike a more elaborate global coordination system.
assumptions: Tenant quotas can be apportioned among regions and rebalanced asynchronously based on recent demand.
The local burst allowance is bounded by tenant entitlement and regional shared-capacity headroom.
The regional limiter can be implemented as a single new stateful service or by extending an existing supported dependency.
Small, bounded temporary global-quota overshoot during partitions is acceptable.
risks: Static regional allocations may falsely throttle a tenant whose traffic shifts rapidly between regions.
Local burst allowances across all three regions can produce bounded global quota overshoot.
Fail-open behavior during an 11-minute-scale outage could pressure regional capacity if safety caps are too generous.
Regional limiter state loss or hot-key load from the largest tenants could impair enforcement.
Quota allocation, rebalancing, and partition behavior add more complexity than uncoordinated per-instance buckets.

citations.claim: The top 2 percent of tenants generate 61 percent of peak request volume, supporting tenant-isolated enforcement.
Bursts frequently reach 4 times the five-minute average for under 20 seconds, supporting local burst capacity.
Cross-region control-plane round trips have 180 ms p99 latency, making request-path global coordination undesirable.
A regional dependency outage lasted 11 minutes while application instances remained healthy, supporting partition-tolerant local enforcement.
The platform team can support at most one new stateful dependency.
Tenant entitlement data is already replicated regionally and can provide quota inputs without a new global lookup.
